topic: Roblox responsive GUI layout and safe-area APIs/guidance

claims.claim: Scale-relative sizing is preferable to fixed Offset sizing for UI intended to respond across multiple screen resolutions.
claims.scope: On-screen GuiObject position and size expressed with UDim2 across varying viewport sizes; this is comparative guidance, not a universal engine requirement.
limitations: Roblox says many UI elements scale more responsively with percentage-based Scale values, not that every size or position must use Scale.
The same official tutorial says strict pixel values are useful in certain cases; offsets remain appropriate for fixed padding, minimum/maximum bounds, and other intentionally pixel-sized details.
Scale alone does not guarantee a usable layout across different aspect ratios; Roblox separately recommends testing multiple emulated device categories.

sources.title: Create HUD meters — Position the frame / Resize the frame
sources.supports: Defines Scale as a percentage of the container and Offset as pixels; calls Scale the best approach for edge-relative positioning and says many UI elements scale more responsively across multiple screens when sized as a percentage, while acknowledging strict pixels can be useful.

sources.title: Create score bars — Test the design
sources.supports: Explains that differing viewport aspect ratios require validation across screen sizes and instructs creators to test at least one phone, tablet, desktop, and console device.

claims.claim: Size constraints can bound responsive UI elements.
claims.scope: GuiObjects with a child UISizeConstraint; bounds are pixel-valued MinSize and MaxSize limits applied after responsive sizing/layout calculations.
limitations: UISizeConstraint bounds are expressed in pixels, even when the GuiObject's base Size uses Scale.
When a UILayout also controls the object, the constraint determines the minimum/maximum size and overrides a layout-applied size at those bounds.
This establishes capability, not a rule that every responsive element should have a UISizeConstraint.

sources.title: UISizeConstraint API reference
sources.supports: States that UISizeConstraint prevents a GuiObject from becoming larger than MaxSize or smaller than MinSize and defines both properties as pixel bounds.

sources.title: Create HUD meters — Constrain the size
sources.supports: Shows a Scale-sized meter becoming too tall on tablet/older-phone aspect ratios, then applies UISizeConstraint.MaxSize to cap its height at 20 pixels.

sources.title: Create score bars — Create the frame
sources.supports: Uses UISizeConstraint.MinSize so a responsive score bar never shrinks below 40 pixels vertically and remains legible on smaller screens.

claims.claim: Safe-area/inset handling is required so interactive UI is not obscured by device cutouts or Roblox system UI.
claims.scope: Interactive or information-bearing descendants of ScreenGui on displays with cutouts and where Roblox Core UI/top-bar controls occupy screen space.
limitations: The required outcome—keeping accessible UI clear of obstructions—is supported, but explicit custom inset code or configuration is not universally required: ScreenGui.ScreenInsets defaults to CoreUISafeInsets, which automatically keeps descendants clear of Roblox Core UI and device cutouts.

ScreenInsets.None is intentionally available. Roblox says it should only be used for ScreenGuis containing noninteractive content such as background images, so the rule is not universal for all GUI content.
DeviceSafeInsets avoids hardware cutouts but does not automatically reserve every Core UI control; the official HUD example relies on right alignment to remain clear of Roblox UI.

ClipToDeviceSafeArea controls clipping and defaults true; disabling it can allow descendants to be obscured. SafeAreaCompatibility provides legacy fullscreen transformations, but Roblox recommends ScreenInsets for new work.

sources.title: ScreenGui API reference — ScreenInsets, ClipToDeviceSafeArea, SafeAreaCompatibility, IgnoreGuiInset
sources.supports: Documents that CoreUISafeInsets is the default and keeps descendants clear of top-bar buttons and camera notches; warns that None can place UI behind Core UI/cutouts and should only be used for noninteractive content; documents clipping and compatibility behavior.

sources.title: Create HUD meters — Utilize safe areas
sources.supports: Says modern phones have notches/cutouts and every Roblox game has top-bar controls; presents ScreenInsets as the mechanism to ensure UI remains visible and accessible, and contrasts CoreUISafeInsets with DeviceSafeInsets.

sources.title: GuiService API reference — GetGuiInset and TopbarInset
sources.supports: Provides pixel inset values through GetGuiInset and a dynamic TopbarInset for UI that must react to currently unoccupied top-bar space; TopbarInset may change with Core UI visibility.

claims.claim: 667×375 is an official Roblox responsive-UI validation target.
claims.scope: Current Roblox Creator Hub/API documentation, official samples surfaced by Context7, and exact-term web fallback searches as of the access date.
limitations: No current authoritative source located names 667×375 as a required, recommended, or canonical validation resolution.
The official score-bar guide instead requires testing at least one device from each of Phone, Tablet, Desktop, and Console, without naming 667×375.
The current HUD-meter guide gives iPhone X and Samsung Galaxy A51 as example phone presets and says the Device Emulator supports custom presets; examples are not universal validation targets.
A not-found verdict does not prove the resolution was never present in an older Studio preset or never used by the community.

sources.title: Create score bars — Test the design
sources.supports: Defines the current validation guidance as using Actual Resolution and testing at least one Phone, Tablet, Desktop, and Console device; it does not identify 667×375.

sources.title: Create HUD meters — Enable the Device Emulator
sources.supports: Calls the Device Emulator the best way to test UI across platforms, notes preset and custom devices, and names iPhone X or Samsung Galaxy A51 only as example phone emulations; it does not establish 667×375 as a target.

sources.title: Studio testing modes — Device emulation
sources.supports: Provides the official device-emulation mechanism for cross-device testing; no authoritative 667×375 validation requirement was surfaced from this documentation through Context7 or exact-term web fallback.

conflicts: Generic responsive guidance supports preferring Scale for many multi-resolution elements, but it does not support converting that preference into an engine-level MUST or banning Offset.

Safe-area avoidance is strong official guidance for interactive UI, while the engine already applies CoreUISafeInsets by default and explicitly permits ScreenInsets.None for noninteractive backgrounds; therefore 'authors must always implement custom inset handling' conflicts with the API's defaults and exceptions.
Community references may use 667×375 as a practical small-phone test case, but no current official source located elevates it to a Roblox validation target.
unresolved: Context7 was used first with /websites/create_roblox. It returned current responsive-sizing, constraint, safe-area, and emulator guidance but no material naming 667×375. Web search was then used as the required fallback for that gap; exact searches did not locate a current Creator Hub, official sample, or Roblox staff source establishing 667×375 as an official target.
Whether 667×375 corresponds to a historically shipped Device Emulator preset was not established by current authoritative documentation.
